topics.title: History compression with task-conditioned representation
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can joint history compression and task-conditioned representation improve click AUC over both frozen source bests at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: History compression and task-conditioned representation may preserve complementary predictive signals. A joint approach should exceed the stronger source when compared with both frozen sources, component replacement controls and matched-capacity alternatives. Failure to exceed the stronger source, or an advantage explained by added capacity or compute, would falsify useful complementarity for the tested implementation; no mechanism is established by the existing summaries.

topics.title: Conditional utility of historical action codes
topics.question: Under the frozen inputs, history policy and training protocol, do historical action codes improve click AUC beyond aligned historical item content and task-mask membership in the strongest visible model, at justified parameter and measured runtime cost?
topics.hypothesis: Historical action codes may carry useful feedback beyond item fields and task-mask memberships, but the supplied evidence does not isolate this contribution. Inherit the strongest visible trial unchanged as the utility control. Compare full action use with an action-blind representation and a counts-only replacement while retaining representation capacity, all other fields, event order, task masks, training objectives and exposure. If actions vary within membership strata, permute only historical actions within those strata to preserve action counts and membership associations while testing event alignment; absent variation, record that this contrast is uninformative. Keep host history construction, padding and the unknown target action unchanged. Full-use superiority over replacements would provisionally support conditional utility; equivalence or improvement after removal would undermine it. Counts-only equivalence would favor frequency over alignment, while capacity or optimization differences remain alternative explanations. Measure parameters and local training/inference time, repeat informative comparisons within the authorized protocol, and reserve assessment resources. No mechanism or novelty claim is established by the compact evidence.

decisions.reason: Current representation topic gained 0.000951 AUC after 24 attempts; all four recent trials remain below its best. Merge to test complementarity, retaining both frozen source bests as utility controls and requiring improvement over 0.660647 AUC with parameter, training and inference cost accounting and matched-capacity controls. Compatibility and mechanisms remain unresolved; single-seed gains are provisional.

These single-seed observations warrant continuing attribution through component replacement and matched-capacity/exposure controls, plus independent-seed repetitions against both frozen sources. The joint best exceeds the stronger frozen source by 0.001211 AUC with fewer parameters and lower recorded inference time. Continue the current question with both frozen source controls, component replacements, matched-capacity comparisons, repetition and measured costs; useful complementarity remains provisional.

The joint best reaches 0.666900 AUC versus the stronger source's 0.666199, with 32.13M versus 56.35M parameters and reported inference of 26.00 versus 33.48 seconds. This single-seed advantage supports continued attribution, not confirmed complementarity. Recent auxiliary variants form two identical metric pairs and add no independent replication. Prioritize compression-by-task-conditioning replacement controls and matched-capacity alternatives, retaining both frozen source bests and measuring cost. Loss of the advantage under these controls would falsify useful complementarity; reserve repetition and assessment resources. Deepen joint-model attribution. The joint best exceeds the stronger frozen source by 0.000812 AUC. This suggests an unresolved interaction, not confirmed complementarity. None of four recent equal-parameter trials exceeds it. Continue component-replacement and matched-capacity/cost contrasts against both frozen sources; loss of the advantage under these controls would falsify useful complementarity. Continue to resolve complementarity using both frozen source controls, component replacements, matched-capacity comparisons and measured costs, reserving resources for repetition. The joint best (AUC 0.668527) exceeds both frozen source bests (0.667268 and 0.664539). Recent transfer variants exceed their blocked counterparts by 0.000659 and 0.000773 at equal parameter counts and similar measured runtime, but neither improves the best. Continue attribution with both frozen source controls and matched-capacity/cost comparisons: useful complementarity remains provisional, and replacement controls could explain the advantage without the proposed mechanism.

Joint best exceeds the stronger frozen source by 0.001259 AUC with 32.19M versus 56.42M parameters and 28.72 versus 41.96 seconds inference. Recent activation replacements lose AUC; the identical same-seed result is not independent replication. Continue with both frozen source bests and component replacement controls matched for capacity and measured cost, reserving budget for attribution. Recent transfer/blocked pairs show provisional AUC advantages of 0.000337 and 0.000378 at identical parameter counts; neither exceeds the current 0.668527 best. Their 383–405 second training costs leave room for discriminating replacement and measured-cost controls. Deepen the current question by testing whether the apparent transfer benefit survives those controls; compact summaries do not establish intervention isolation or a mechanism, and loss of the advantage would falsify this lead.

The joint best exceeds both frozen source bests, but mechanism support remains provisional. Restored/native bridge AUC differs by only 0.00000494; both isolated variants reach 0.668038, below the 0.668532 best. Deepen the existing representation-complementarity question with matched replacement controls and repetition; these trial names do not establish the mechanism. Retain native and unchanged-best controls, both source bests, and the stronger auxiliary result (0.668961) as utility comparisons. Require gains to survive capacity and measured-cost controls; reserve attribution and assessment resources within the remaining 40,949 seconds. Compatibility with auxiliary changes remains unresolved.

After 281 attempts, all four recent variants regress and cost more inference time; the strongest visible comparator reaches 0.668961. Continue with both frozen source controls, the unchanged joint best, component-replacement and matched-capacity/cost controls, reserving budget for repetition and assessment. Complementarity remains unverified: loss of the advantage under replacement controls or repetition would undermine it. The summaries do not establish compatibility with other topics strongly enough to justify another merge.

Historical action utility remains unidentified in the compact evidence and is distinct from the active membership, order and auxiliary-supervision questions.
